tasks.short: Develop database architectures and keep their documentation consistent

steps.what: Inspect current database schemas, interface contracts and approved architecture requirements
inputs: database-owned schema metadata and access definitions
application-owner interface contracts and approved requirements
outputs: checked architecture inputs and gaps

steps.what: Develop the database architecture model with entities, dependencies, ownership and deployment boundaries
inputs: checked architecture inputs and gaps
outputs: architect-authored structured database architecture model

steps.what: Document the model's entity catalogue, relationships and deployment diagrams in the architecture document
inputs: architect-authored structured database architecture model
outputs: draft architecture tables and diagrams tied to model version

steps.what: Write the architecture rationale, rejected alternatives and unresolved design risks
inputs: architect-authored structured database architecture model
draft architecture tables and diagrams tied to model version
outputs: complete architecture document with human-written rationale

steps.what: Verify the model and document agree and approve the final architecture document version
inputs: complete architecture document with human-written rationale
architect-authored structured database architecture model
outputs: approved architecture document v1

steps.what: Save the approved architecture document version in its internal document record
inputs: approved architecture document v1
outputs: stored architecture document version

tasks.design: Use read-only metadata views from the {DATA_PLATFORM} and native exports from the {OTHER} database modelling tool to populate tables and diagrams in the {DOCS}. The architect develops the model, writes its rationale and approves a consistent final document before saving it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Architecture views and documentation can diverge when diagrams and catalogues are maintained separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Native model exports can render declared entities and relationships without a language model.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing appropriate boundaries and explaining trade-offs requires understanding the application and organisation.
tasks.human_edge: Judge when a technically valid model encodes the wrong business ownership or dependency.

ambition.what: Review architecture drift against the approved model before each significant application interface change.

reach.task: Review trust boundaries in the database design
reach.learn: Threat modelling and ownership of privileged access.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-5 for read-only metadata access and permitted schema disclosure

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: database modelling tools can export schema-derived catalogues and relationship diagrams from structured models.

assumptions: Boundary is architecture development and documentation, not deploying the database. OTHER means the database modelling tool. Overlap with strategy and application-design tasks must be reconciled in roll-up, not counted twice.

Database owners supply schema name, object id, columns, keys, access definitions and extraction version. Application owners supply approved interface requirements. Missing definitions are checked manually in s1 and authored in s2; no free model creation is assumed.

The model in s2 is the input contract for s3: entity ids, attributes, relationship endpoints, deployment node and owner. Native export configuration is tested first; narrative rationale remains human.
Shares and savings are provisional scenarios, not observed baselines. Same-system saving has approximately no effort today and remains fully retained at one-point granularity.
unknowns: Existing model export and current-document integration
research_questions: Does a native export preserve one architecture's declared versus observed relationships?
How much document assembly remains after model authoring?

already_counted.description: Inspect exported diagrams and tables for omissions and readability

incremental.description: Maintain export layout and metadata mappings

approvals.approved_version: approved architecture document v1; edits require s5 again

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 21 minus 1 upkeep gives 20. High allows four more hours correcting export omissions; low covers existing automatic documentation or incompatible models.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate to understand database business requirements

steps.what: Review existing business requirements and application context before collaborating with system architects, software architects and design analysts
inputs: stakeholder-maintained requirements with ids, owners and versions
existing application context documents
outputs: checked collaboration agenda and source references

steps.what: Collaborate with system architects, software architects, design analysts and others to understand business or industry requirements
inputs: checked collaboration agenda and source references
actual stakeholder explanations and examples
outputs: actual requirement clarifications and unresolved disagreements
steps.handoff_to: system architects, software architects and design analysts

steps.what: Capture clarified requirements, their owners, examples and open questions in the requirements record
inputs: actual requirement clarifications and unresolved disagreements
checked collaboration agenda and source references
outputs: completed draft requirement clarification record

steps.what: Check attribution and uncertainty and approve the final clarification record without treating open issues as agreed requirements
inputs: completed draft requirement clarification record
outputs: approved clarification record v1

steps.what: Save the approved clarification record in its existing requirements system
inputs: approved clarification record v1
outputs: stored requirement clarifications

tasks.design: Configure a requirements view and linked clarification form in the {PROJECT}, with references to current documents in the {DOCS}. The architect holds the collaboration and captures actual meaning, using prefilled identifiers and owner fields rather than an assumed meeting transcript.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated lookup and copying requirement identifiers can add effort around substantive conversations.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked records can prefill existing identifiers and versions while leaving new clarifications to the person.
tasks.still_hard: Stakeholders may mean different things by the same business term or disagree about priority.
tasks.human_edge: Elicit examples and expose disagreement before it hardens into an incorrect schema.

ambition.what: No new decision rights are assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3 for project and document access; consult participants if recording practices change

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: linked requirements forms can reuse source identifiers and owner fields without generating a conversation's meaning.

assumptions: Boundary includes meeting preparation, actual collaboration and its written clarification record. Other participants' time remains outside the focal denominator and earns no claimed saving.
Requirement owners already maintain id, version, owner and document link. If absent, s1 includes manual lookup and s3 includes capture; native configuration must be tried before custom code.
s3 retains fourteen hours for actual semantic capture, examples and corrections; only reuse of existing metadata reduces time. No free transcript, approval or statement of consensus is assumed.
Shares and retained percentages are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. s5 is an approximately zero-effort same-system save and remains fully retained.
unknowns: Existing requirement ownership and linking discipline
Actual time spent copying identifiers versus writing meaning
research_questions: Does a linked form reduce record preparation while preserving unresolved disagreement?
Can the architect locate a clarification's exact source version?

already_counted.description: Write and check actual clarifications and metadata

incremental.description: Maintain clarification form links and required fields

approvals.approved_version: approved clarification record v1; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 11 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 10.5. High allows 2.5 further hours of source and metadata correction; low applies where native linked forms already cover the work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop database strategies across modelling, design and implementation

steps.what: Inspect business requirements, current database capabilities and implementation constraints
inputs: approved requirement versions and owners
database inventory and measured workload summaries maintained by database operations
outputs: checked strategy evidence and missing constraints

steps.what: Clarify business priorities and implementation constraints with application and operations owners
inputs: checked strategy evidence and missing constraints
actual owner explanations
outputs: clarified priorities and practical constraints

steps.what: Develop database architectural strategies for the modelling, design and implementation stages and record explicit option assumptions
inputs: checked strategy evidence and missing constraints
clarified priorities and practical constraints
outputs: architect-authored strategy alternatives and numeric scenario inputs

steps.what: Calculate comparable capacity and cost scenarios for the authored strategy alternatives
inputs: architect-authored strategy alternatives and numeric scenario inputs
checked strategy evidence and missing constraints
outputs: checked scenario calculations and assumption sensitivities

steps.what: Select a recommended strategy and write its stage-specific rationale, dependencies and risks
inputs: architect-authored strategy alternatives and numeric scenario inputs
checked scenario calculations and assumption sensitivities
outputs: complete database architecture strategy recommendation

steps.what: Check and approve the exact final strategy recommendation for the architecture record
inputs: complete database architecture strategy recommendation
outputs: approved strategy recommendation v1

steps.what: Save the approved strategy recommendation in its existing internal architecture record
inputs: approved strategy recommendation v1
outputs: stored strategy recommendation

tasks.design: Configure requirement and workload views in the {PROJECT} and {DATA_PLATFORM}, and reusable scenario formulas in the {SPREADSHEET}. The architect supplies option assumptions, develops stage-specific strategies and writes the recommendation in the {DOCS}; formulas calculate quantities rather than choose the strategy.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparing alternatives can require repeated navigation and rebuilding the same capacity and cost formulas.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing views and protected scenario sheets can reuse approved inputs and expose assumptions.
tasks.still_hard: Growth, migration constraints and organisational priorities are uncertain and cannot be reduced to a cost ranking.
tasks.human_edge: Choose which risks are tolerable and identify when a cheap architecture creates an unacceptable dependency.

ambition.what: Revisit the preferred migration strategy when a major workload assumption changes.

reach.learn: Sensitivity analysis and cost allocation without presenting forecasts as measurements.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-4 for workload and cost access; consult owners about permitted use

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: protected scenario spreadsheets can calculate comparable capacity and cost outcomes from explicitly entered assumptions.

assumptions: Boundary is architectural strategy development and recording, not subsequent production implementation or executive investment approval. The architect approves the recommendation as their work, not the organisation's spend.

Operations supplies timestamped workload measures and inventory identifiers; requirement owners supply ids and versions. Missing evidence and manual capture remain in s1-s3. s3 explicitly captures scenario inputs, units and cost basis before s4 uses them.
Native views and formulas first. No language model chooses strategies or performs arithmetic. Existing system runtime is not counted labour.

Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not observed baselines. Same-system saving stays fully retained. Overlapping requirement review and architecture modelling must be reconciled with neighbouring tasks in roll-up.
unknowns: Quality of workload and cost inputs
Existing scenario sheets and decision process
research_questions: Can two existing strategy alternatives be reproduced from explicit inputs?
Which assumptions dominate the decision when varied?

already_counted.description: Check scenario formulas, units and sensitivities

incremental.description: Maintain scenario formulas and source mappings

approvals.approved_version: approved strategy recommendation v1; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 13.2 minus 1 upkeep gives 12.2. High allows 3.2 additional hours for inconsistent scenario inputs; low applies where existing views and formulas already cover the work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design application databases for scalability, security, performance and reliability

steps.what: Inspect business application data contracts, workload examples and scalability, security, performance and reliability requirements
inputs: application-owner data contracts and representative read queries
operations-owned workload observations and service requirements
outputs: checked database design requirements and workload evidence

steps.what: Design databases to support business applications, choosing data structures, access paths, security boundaries and reliability provisions
inputs: checked database design requirements and workload evidence
outputs: architect-authored logical and physical database model with explicit constraints and access design

steps.what: Prepare the draft schema definition from the chosen physical model without executing it
inputs: architect-authored logical and physical database model with explicit constraints and access design
outputs: draft schema definition tied to design model version

steps.what: Inspect existing representative read-query plans and compare observed workload measures with explicit design constraints
inputs: checked database design requirements and workload evidence
architect-authored logical and physical database model with explicit constraints and access design
existing read-query plans supplied by database operations
outputs: checked plan comparisons and unmet or untested design requirements

steps.what: Assess scalability, security, performance and reliability trade-offs and finish the design with unresolved tests explicit
inputs: draft schema definition tied to design model version
checked plan comparisons and unmet or untested design requirements
architect-authored logical and physical database model with explicit constraints and access design
outputs: complete application database design packet with outstanding validation needs

steps.what: Check consistency and approve the final database design packet for the internal design record
inputs: complete application database design packet with outstanding validation needs
outputs: approved application database design packet v1

steps.what: Save the approved final application database design packet without deploying its schema
inputs: approved application database design packet v1
outputs: stored application database design version

tasks.design: Use native model-to-schema export in the {OTHER} database modelling tool and configured read-only workload views in the {DATA_PLATFORM}. The architect authors the physical model, checks generated definitions and interprets the evidence before approving the complete design in the {DOCS}; this workflow executes no schema changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Typing schema definitions and navigating workload evidence can duplicate information already present in a structured model.
tasks.enabler_now: Native schema generators and workload views expose declared structures and observed query behaviour without a model loop.
tasks.still_hard: Existing query plans cannot prove that an unbuilt design meets future reliability or security needs.
tasks.human_edge: Identify untested assumptions, security boundaries and failure modes rather than treating a plausible schema as validated.

ambition.what: Compare a second physical design when a significant application workload changes.

reach.task: Examine data access boundaries in an application design

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-5 for model and read-only workload access; restrict query parameters containing personal data

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: structured database modelling tools can generate schema definitions, and database monitoring views expose existing query plans and workload observations.

assumptions: Boundary is application database design, including schema preparation and evidence review, not production deployment or actual resilience testing. Unperformed tests remain explicit, not silently passed.

OTHER is a database modelling tool. Application owners provide query text, purpose and contract version; operations provides dated workload measures and existing query plans. Missing evidence is manually sought in s1/s4, or marked unavailable; no machine step assumes a free benchmark run.

s2 explicitly creates entities, fields, keys, indexes and constraints before schema generation. Native export and workload views first; unsupported clauses are written and checked manually within retained s3 time.

Shares and savings are provisional scenarios, not measurements. The same-system save remains fully retained and contributes no saving. Overlapping architecture outputs with other tasks require roll-up ownership reconciliation.
unknowns: Native generator coverage of the actual schema dialect
Whether workload samples represent peak demand
Which security and reliability tests remain necessary
research_questions: Does a generated definition preserve every authored constraint in a reviewed design?
Do observed query plans cover the application's important access patterns?

already_counted.description: Check generated definitions against authored keys, types and constraints
Check workload and plan comparisons and identify missing evidence

incremental.description: Maintain schema export settings and workload view mappings

approvals.approved_version: approved application database design packet v1; changes require s6 again

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 22.2 minus 2 upkeep gives 20.2. High allows 4.2 extra hours for unsupported clauses and unrepresentative workload evidence; low applies where existing tooling already performs the same exports and views.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The architect spends less time transferring model definitions into documents and finding known requirements, while retaining architecture choices and the duty to expose untested assumptions.
reach: Review data trust boundaries with information security after learning threat modelling.
Compare staged infrastructure choices with finance after learning cost sensitivity analysis.
skills_to_grow: Distinguish observed workload evidence from design forecasts
role.ambitious_version: Bring explicit workload, cost and security assumptions to architecture decisions early enough to compare a second feasible design.
